page: Microsoft Azure D16pls_v5 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the DPLSv5 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs powered by an Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 3.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include any local storage or GPU hardware, though it is premium storage capable.

Benchmark evaluations show average multi-core capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 28902.52 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 9624.0. Memory read bandwidth is measured at 1127.02 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 126.1 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. However, single-core and specialized execution paths show weaknesses. The Geekbench single-core score of 1111.0 and bzip3 single-threaded decompression speed of 8.82 GB/sec fall into the lower performance tier. Cryptographic performance is also limited, as evidenced by a weak Passmark CPU encryption score of 2592.32, despite hardware-level AES support.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM64 architecture combined with a lower memory-to-core ratio provides a resource-dense option for workloads that do not require high memory allocations. Tradeoffs include the lack of local storage, absence of hyperthreading, and lower single-threaded performance. This server is suited for multi-threaded applications, static web serving, software compilation, and database operations such as Redis, which recorded 21.72 million operations per second.
